# Testament of Dan — 7
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1:1** The copy of the words of Dan, which he spoke to his sons in his last days, in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life.
**1:2** For he called his family together and said: Hearken to my words, ye sons of Dan; and give heed to the words of your father.
**1:3** I have proved in my heart and in my whole life that truth with just dealing is good and well-pleasing to God, and that lying and anger are evil.
**1:4** And I confess to you this day, my children, that in my heart I resolved to kill Joseph my brother, because the spirit of jealousy and vainglory said to me: Thou also art his son.
**1:5** And one of the spirits of Beliar stirred me up, saying: Take this sword, and with it slay Joseph; so shall thy father love thee when he is dead.
**1:6** Now the spirit of anger sought to persuade me to crush Joseph as a leopard crushes a kid.
**1:7** But the God of my fathers did not suffer him to fall into my hands, so that I found him not when I sought him; and lest I should work iniquity in Israel, he removed him from among us.

**2:1** And now, my children, behold I am dying, and I tell you in truth: unless ye keep yourselves from the spirit of lying and of anger, and love truth and long-suffering, ye shall perish.
**2:2** For anger is blindness, and suffers not one to see the face of any man with truth.
**2:3** For though it be a father or a mother, he behaves toward them as enemies; though it be a brother, he knows him not; though it be a prophet of the Lord, he disobeys him; though it be a righteous man, he regards him not; though it be a friend, he does not acknowledge him.
**2:4** For the spirit of anger encompasses him with the net of deceit, and blinds his natural eyes, and through lying darkens his mind, and gives him its own peculiar vision.
**2:5** And wherewith does it encompass his eyes? With hatred of heart, so as to be jealous of his brother.

**3:1** For anger is an evil thing, my children, for it troubles even the soul itself.
**3:2** And the body of the angry man it makes its own, and over his soul it gets the mastery, and it bestows upon the body power that it may work all iniquity.
**3:3** And when the body does all these things, the soul justifies what is done, since it sees not aright.
**3:4** Therefore he that is wrathful, if he be a mighty man, has a threefold power in his anger: first by the help of his servants; secondly by his wealth whereby he persuades and overcomes wrongfully; and thirdly having his own natural power.
**3:5** But though the wrathful man be weak, yet has he a power twofold of that which is by nature; for wrath ever aids such in lawlessness.
**3:6** This spirit goes always with lying at the right hand of Satan, that with cruelty and lying his works may be wrought.

**4:1** Understand therefore the power of wrath, that it is vain; for it first of all gives provocation by word; then by deeds it strengthens him who is angry, and with sharp losses disturbs his mind, and so with great wrath it stirs up his soul unto destruction.
**4:2** When therefore any one speaks against you, be not moved to anger; and if any man praises you as holy men, be not uplifted.
**4:3** For first it pleases the hearing, and so sharpens the mind, and then being enraged he thinks that he is justly angered.
**4:4** If ye fall into any loss or ruin, my children, be not afflicted; for this very spirit makes a man desire that which is perishable, in order that he may be enraged through the affliction.
**4:5** For if ye bring against him losses or destruction of that in which he delights, he is maddened, and from the madness he begets hatred, and from hatred he proceeds to enmity, from enmity to murder, and murder to death.

**5:1** Therefore flee the evil imagination also, by seeing beforehand the temptation of Beliar; flee from all lying, and love truth.
**5:2** Keep the law of the Lord, and depart from all anger; and love truth and long-suffering.
**5:3** And the things ye have heard from your father, tell also to your children, that the Savior of the nations may receive you; for he is true and long-suffering, meek and humble, and teaches by his works the law of God.
**5:4** Depart therefore from all unrighteousness, and cleave to the righteousness of God; and your race shall be saved for ever, and our father shall rejoice over you.

**6:1** And behold I have told you all things, that I might be acquitted of your sin.
**6:2** For if ye depart from the evil, and cleave to the good, then shall the Lord dwell among you; because he loved Jacob our father and all his seed.
**6:3** But I know that in the last days ye will depart from the Lord, and will be scattered in all nations, and among the enemies of Israel shall ye be dispersed.
**6:4** And after this, if ye return to the Lord in truth and with all your heart, he will gather you out of all the nations, whither the Lord your God shall have scattered you.

**7:1** But when ye turn to the Lord with all your heart, being humble and meek, then shall the Lord come to you working salvation to all the nations.
**7:2** And he shall make war against Beliar and shall execute an everlasting vengeance on our enemies; and the captivity shall he take from Beliar, even the souls of the saints, and shall turn disobedient hearts unto the Lord, and shall give to them that call upon him eternal peace.
**7:3** And when he had said these things he kissed them and fell asleep; and his sons buried him in Hebron.

---
*End of Testament of Dan*
